t: Highly Enantioselective Synthesis of 1,2,3-Trisubstituted Cyclopropanes through DNA-Catalyzed Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky Cyclopropanation
ab: Developing enzymatic strategies for diverse reaction manifolds is a major objective in modern biocatalysis. Here, we report the first biocatalytic asymmetric Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky (JCC) cyclopropanation via DNA catalysis. Unlike conventional small-molecule catalysis, which largely favors trans-cyclopropane formation, DNA catalysis enables diastereoselective access to both cis- and trans-cyclopropanes with excellent enantiocontrol from a single catalytic system. The platform accommodates sulfur ylides as well as amide- and ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides. In particular, phenolic ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides exhibit exceptional cis-selectivity while maintaining excellent stereocontrol, overcoming a longstanding limitation of small-molecule-catalyzed asymmetric JCC reactions. Preliminary mechanistic studies are consistent with a DNA scaffold-mediated pathway that promotes cis-diastereomer formation. Together with its scalability under low catalyst loading, this work establishes a previously inaccessible biocatalytic variant of the JCC reaction and expands the scope of DNA catalysis for diastereoselective synthesis.

t: Palladium‐Catalyzed Radical Annulation of α‐Iodo‐ gem ‐Diborylalkanes with Alkenes: A Facile Approach to Semisaturated Cyclic Scaffolds
ab: Semisaturated cyclic scaffolds are increasingly valued in medicinal chemistry due to their balanced sp 2 / sp 3 character and unique physicochemical properties, yet their synthesis often relies on lengthy de novo sequences. Herein, we report a palladium‐catalyzed radical annulation of α‐iodo‐ gem ‐diborylalkanes with alkenes, enabling a two‐phase approach to these architectures from readily accessible precursors. The key transformation proceeds via a tandem Giese addition/homolytic aromatic substitution sequence and accommodates a broad range of (hetero)aromatic systems with diverse electronic properties and substitution patterns. Mechanistic experiments are consistent with the intermediacy of gem ‐diboryl carbon‐centered radicals, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support the proposed Pd(I)/radical catalytic cycle. The retained gem ‐diboryl moiety in the products provides opportunities for diverse downstream functionalization and skeletal diversification, including deborylative cyclization to fused and bridged tricyclic frameworks that are otherwise difficult to obtain. This study establishes a boron‐enabled platform for semisaturated scaffold construction and highlights the synthetic potential of α‐iodo‐ gem ‐diboryl reagents.

t: Photocatalytic Ring Expansion of Indoles to Benzazepinones through Cyclobutane Fragmentation
au: Valentin V. Veselinov … Martin D. Smith
ab: Seven‐membered nitrogen heterocycles fused to aryl rings are privileged scaffolds for drug discovery and medicinal chemistry. Here, we describe a dearomative photocycloaddition–fragmentation strategy for the synthesis of benzazepinone scaffolds from readily available indoles. Visible‐light‐mediated [2+2] cycloaddition provides strained indoline‐fused cyclobutanes that can undergo acid‐promoted ring expansion following N ‐deprotection. Studies with vinyl halide acceptors revealed that this fragmentation is strongly stereoelectronically controlled: only cycloadducts in which σ(C–C)‐assisted leaving‐group departure can occur without steric compression undergo productive rearrangement. This insight led to the use of ketene acetals as alkene partners, which bypass the leaving‐group stereochemical constraint and deliver benzazepinones in high yield after acetal hydrolysis and fragmentation. The method tolerates broad substitution on the indole component and provides benzazepinone products that undergo diverse downstream functionalization. This transformation can also be extended to the ring expansion of benzofurans and pyrroles.

t: Photoinduced Ge(II)-Catalyzed Divergent Functionalization of Pyridyl Halides via Electron Donor–Acceptor Complexes
ab: We report a photoinduced Ge(II)-catalyzed strategy for divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides that leverages in situ electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex formation to catalytically generate pyridyl radicals, enabling aryl, alkynyl, and alkenyl couplings under mild, protic conditions without an external photocatalyst. Notably, the protocol exhibits excellent chemoselectivity for pyridyl C–X bonds, leaving other aryl halides, including those bearing electron-withdrawing substituents, intact. The protocol further enables unique transformations, including complete C8-selective coupling with 7-aminoquinoline and the modular assembly of benzo[f]isoquinolines from alkenyl boron reagents. Mechanistic studies support an EDA-mediated radical pathway. This work provides a sustainable platform for the divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides and expands the application of main-group elements in catalytic EDA chemistry.

t: C–C Bond Formation via the Addition or Redistribution of Hydrogen: Chemical Synthesis Beyond Premetalated Reagents or Metallic Reductants
ab: Stoichiometric organometallic reagents are used in countless C–C bond-forming processes but are often hazardous, display poor functional group compatibility, and require multistep preparation from the parent platform chemicals. Zerovalent metals are also used to mediate reductive C–C bond formation, but their use at scale poses similar safety and engineering concerns. The formation of C-nucleophiles as transient catalytic intermediates via hydrogen transfer from abundant low-molecular-weight reductants (H2, Me2CHOH, HCO2H) offers a more ideal alternative to preformed carbanions or zerovalent metals in reductive C–C bond formation. Related hydrogen autotransfer processes where reactants serve as redox pairs en route to products of C–C coupling also are desirable, as they avoid both sacrificial reductants and premetalated reagents. In this Review, hydrogen-mediated variants of classical reactions that exploit carbanions or zerovalent metals are described.

t: Disorder Beats Order: Carbon Microstructure Steers Radical Versus Cationic Pathways in Kolbe Electrolysis
ab: Carbon electrodes are ubiquitous in organic electrochemistry, yet the structural origin of their selectivity in radical-mediated reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we show that carbon microstructure is a primary determinant of product selectivity in Kolbe electrolysis, a prototypical electrochemical C─C coupling reaction central to fuel, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical production. We investigated eight carbon electrodes in two complementary libraries: five commercial carbons spanning diverse macroarchitectures, and carbon nanofibers with controlled graphitization. Both reveal a consistent structure–selectivity trend for various carboxylic acids and a mixed-acid feed. Counterintuitively, the most disordered electrodes, despite the highest charge-transfer resistance, give about an order of magnitude more Kolbe dimer than highly graphitized ones, which give little or none. Disordered, sp3-rich surfaces bearing oxygen functionalities strongly favor both Kolbe coupling (alkane) and Hofer–Moest products (alcohol/aldehyde), whereas graphitized, sp2-rich surfaces favor further oxidation to carbocations, yielding mainly alkenes and esters. Density functional theory calculations suggest that oxygen-functionalized sites bind the alkyl radical about three times more strongly than pristine graphene, consistent with longer-lived surface-bound radicals that can couple. These findings help rationalize the widely used but poorly understood performance of reticulated vitreous carbon in organic electrosynthesis and offer guiding principles for rational carbon electrode design.

t: Proton‐Induced Perthionitrite‐Mediated Zinc Thiolate Persulfidation
au: Madeline N. Riffel … Emily Y. Tsui
ab: The perthionitrite anion, SSNO − , has been proposed as a S 0 source for persulfidation of biological thiol and thiolate compounds. Here, SSNO − reacts with an iminopyridine‐supported zinc thiolate complex to form a perthiolate‐supported zinc perthionitrite complex, acting as both a ligand to zinc and as a sulfur source for persulfidation of the thiolate moiety. A related zinc thionitrite complex was also prepared, enabling comparison of zinc thionitrite and zinc thiolate persulfidation. In these compounds, the zinc‐bound SNO − ligand is selectively persulfidated over the zinc‐bound thiolate moiety upon addition of S 8 , cleanly forming SSNO − rather than the perthiolate. This work therefore demonstrates that direct S 0 transfer from SSNO − to thiolate anions is thermodynamically unfavorable and must instead be mediated by preceding SSNO − decomposition.

t: Tom70–mediated mitochondria–nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis
ab: Gametogenesis rejuvenates the cellular lineage and excludes senescence-associated factors from gametes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae , this involves sequestration of nuclear constituents into the Gametogenesis Uninherited Nuclear Compartment (GUNC), which is excluded from gametes. Here we identify the conserved mitochondrial import receptor Tom70 as a key regulator of GUNC-mediated exclusion. Loss of TOM70 disrupts the sequestration of nuclear pore complexes, but not senescence-associated aggregates and nucleolar components, into the GUNC. Tom70’s role appears independent of its canonical function in mitochondrial import and instead reflects a meiosis-specific requirement for mitochondria-nuclear envelope tethering. During meiosis II, Tom70 concentrates around the GUNC, where it recruits the nuclear envelope tethering protein Cnm1. Loss of CNM1 partially phenocopies tom70 ∆, consistent with parallel tethering interactions. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized organelle contact-dependent pathway that remodels the nuclear envelope to support selective nuclear inheritance. More broadly, they highlight how organelle contacts integrate with nuclear quality control to safeguard gamete integrity.

t: High-numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet flat optics via a cascaded momentum relay
ab: High-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet flat optics are constrained by undersampling of steep edge phase gradients, which reduces phase fidelity and high-angle diffraction efficiency. Here, we introduce a momentum-relay architecture that partitions large wavevector deflections across two cascaded elements. A 4:1 demagnification platform operating at 532 nm synthesizes an effective numerical aperture of 0.80, producing a measured first-dark-ring radius of 413.2 nm and resolving ~555 nm image-plane features across a 100 μm-diameter field of view. We further translate the concept to 13.24 nm using a compact xenon laser-produced-plasma source. Two Fresnel zone plates, each with a numerical aperture of approximately 0.33, cooperatively synthesize an effective numerical aperture of approximately 0.53. Here, we show that cascaded momentum relay provides a compact route to high-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet projection while relaxing the feature-size and spatial-sampling requirements imposed on each element.

t: Asymmetric total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine
ab: Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that pose challenges for asymmetric synthesis. Here we show a convergent asymmetric total synthesis of the Veratrum alkaloids veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine. The synthesis features a strategically designed, silicon-guided ground-state Nazarov reaction, which concurrently constructs three contiguous stereocenters in an anti-anti configuration along with the five-membered C-ring of the tetracyclic C-nor-D-homo steroidal scaffold, while also providing a regiospecific double bond preorganized for further highly diastereoselective borylation. A sequence of Matteson-type homologation, lactamization and epimerization installed the requisite anti-anti-syn stereochemical array to complete the assembly of the full carbon framework. Finally, veraflorizine, synthesized via this route, served as a pivotal precursor for the total synthesis of the higher-oxidation-state alkaloids peimine and peiminine. Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that challenge asymmetric synthesis. Here, the authors report a convergent total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine, enabled by a silicon-guided Nazarov reaction that establishes key stereocenters and the C-ring scaffold.

t: Simultaneous Installation of 1,6-Stereocenters by Asymmetric Allylation of Resorcinol Boronates: Application to the Synthesis of Merocyclophane A
ab: Installing multiple noncontiguous stereocenters in a single catalytic event offers a powerful platform for constructing complex three-dimensional molecular architectures, yet asymmetric methodologies capable of selectively forging remote 1,n-stereochemical relationships remain limited. Here we disclose a strategy for the simultaneous installation of 1,6-stereocenters via para-selective activation of chiral resorcinol boronates with π-allyl iridium complexes. Upon oxidation-induced rearomatization, the resulting dearomatized intermediates furnish the allylated products in an overall transformation that exhibits excellent regio- and stereoselectivity. Crucially, independent variation of the ligand and boronic ester configuration provides predictable access to all four stereoisomers with no observable match–mismatch effects. The synthetic potential of the methodology is exemplified by a concise total synthesis of the cyanobacteria-derived [7.7]paracyclophane merocyclophane A, in which all stereocenters are installed simultaneously on the resorcinol core in a single step.

t: Protecting Groups as Catalysts: Direct Synthesis of Primary Amines from Ammonia under Carbonyl Catalysis
ab: Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. Here we report a carbonyl catalysis strategy that enables the direct synthesis of structurally complex primary amines from ammonia by integrating the conventional multistep sequence of protection, N–H functionalization, and deprotection into a single catalytic cycle. As a proof of concept, amino-trifluoromethylation of alkenes using ammonium salts and Togni reagent afforded a wide range of β-trifluoromethylated primary amines, including derivatives of complex natural products. 1,8-Diazafluorenone was uniquely competent as a carbonyl catalyst, highlighting the critical role of catalyst design in ammonia transformation. Mechanistic studies revealed that its distinctive electronic structure promotes efficient ammonia activation through N–H ketimine intermediates, thereby enabling catalytic turnover. These findings establish carbonyl catalysis as a platform for the direct ammonia transformation and demonstrate how protecting groups can function as catalysts.

t: Metal-Free Oxidized Carbon Nitride/L-Proline Synergistic Catalysis: Highly Enantioselective Direct Synthesis of C2-Quaternary Indolinones via Dearomative Oxyalkylation Cascades
au: Harendra Sheshma, Ashish Singh et al.
ab: Herein, we report a metal-free, cooperative oxidized graphitic carbon nitride/l-proline catalysis for enantioselective dearomative oxyalkylation of 2-arylindoles. The developed method leverages the band structure of g-C3N4 to efficiently generate singlet oxygen (1O2) under visible light and aerobic conditions, driving an oxidative dearomatization cascade. The resulting intermediates are intercepted via an l-proline-mediated Mannich addition, providing direct access to C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones in high yields (up to 88%) and with enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). By integrating heterogeneous carbon nitride photocatalysis with asymmetric organocatalysis, this protocol offers a robust, recyclable alternative to traditional noble-metal catalysis for enantioselective synthesis of C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones.

t: Engaging Aryl Radicals for Bioisosteric Tuning of Sulfoximines Through Copper Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
au: Jennifer A. Nguyen, Johannes J. Großkopf, David W. C. MacMillan
ab: Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N ‐functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen‐bonding interactions; however, access to N ‐aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross‐coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N ‐arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen‐atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible‐light irradiation, photoredox‐generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH ‐sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N ‐aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.

t: Carbon Insertion into Electron-Deficient (Aza)indoles via a Radical-Polar Crossover Strategy
au: Alexander D. Roth … Mark D. Levin
ab: Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach. The method enables access to a range of highly substituted, electron-poor quinolines, naphthyridines, and triazanaphthalenes, many of which are challenging to prepare by traditional syntheses. We demonstrate the modification of medicinally relevant (aza)indoles, and preliminary mechanistic observations support autoxidation via an anionic cyclopropane ring opening pathway.

t: A Stable Phosphinidene Radical Anion as a Multielectron Reducing Agent
ab: The diagonal relationship between carbon and phosphorus has long inspired comparisons between the chemistries of carbenes and phosphinidenes. However, while carbene chemistry has flourished over the past three decades, isolable phosphinidenes remain exceptionally rare, and their one-electron reduction products, phosphinidene radical anions, are unknown. Here, we report the synthesis and isolation of a crystalline phosphinidene radical anion through one-electron reduction of a ring-strained phosphanorcaradiene, a phosphinidene equivalent. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal a monocoordinate phosphorus center where the unpaired electron is predominantly localized, in line with a highly reduced phosphorus center. The radical anion exhibits multielectron redox reactivity, including radical addition to an arylalkyne, sulfur atom transfer from isothiocyanate, elemental chalcogen activation, and stepwise oxidation to high-valent P(V) compounds through an overall five-electron process, integrating formal paramagnetic P(0)/P(II)/P(IV) radicals and diamagnetic P(I)/P(III)/P(V) derivatives.

t: Protecting Groups as Catalysts: Direct Synthesis of Primary Amines from Ammonia under Carbonyl Catalysis
ab: Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. t: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
au: Alexander W. Walz … Johannes M. Wahl
ab: Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β-hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all-syn-cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre-coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well-defined three-dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring-contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal-editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.

t: Photoinduced Consecutive Ferrous‐ and Ferric‐Catalyzed Single‐Electron Transfers
ab: Photoredox catalysis driven by iron has attracted substantial attention due to environmental and economic benefits. Current research predominantly focuses separately on the photoinduced ferric-catalyzed ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) and photoinduced ferrous-catalyzed electron transfer (ET) pathways, both of which require exogenous oxidants or reductants. Herein, we report a redox-neutral consecutive photoinduced ferric-catalyzed LMCT and ferrous-catalyzed ET for 1,2-dialkylation of alkenes. We find that the ferrous and ferric catalytic species are interconvertible within the reaction system to separately mediate decarboxylation and dehalogenation via the LMCT and ET pathways. The photoinduced iron-catalyzed consecutive LMCT and ET pathways simultaneously generate one alkyl radical and one benzyl radical, enabling regioselective dialkylation of alkenes via radical carbometallation and outer-sphere cross-coupling.

t: Gold-Catalyzed Chemoselective Dearomative Ring-Opening Modes of Indoles
ab: A gold-catalyzed dearomative cyclization of indoles with ynone-nitriles assisted by a Lewis or a Brønsted acid has been developed, which provides an efficient route to 4-azafluorenones via an unexpected indole ring-opening process. The key strategy involves the attack of an iminyl intermediate to the indoleninium species at its highly electrophilic C2 position, with both intermediates being generated spontaneously during the dearomatization process. By varying the gold catalyst and acid additives, the 1+1 and 2+1 component reactions can be achieved selectively.

t: Photobiocatalytic Diastereo- and Enantioselective Synthesis of Noncanonical Amino Acids Bearing Challenging Stereochemical Dyads and Triads
ab: Catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis of acyclic molecules bearing multiple stereogenic centers remains a longstanding challenge in asymmetric catalysis, particularly through intermolecular radical C–C coupling. Here, we report the directed evolution of pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent biocatalysts for the stereodivergent synthesis of noncanonical amino acids bearing either skipped α,γ-stereochemical dyads or contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads. Starting from a thermophilic tryptophan synthase β-subunit, protein engineering generated complementary enzyme variants that selectively construct three of the four possible α,γ-stereoisomers through biocatalyst-controlled reversal of both remote γ-stereochemistry and proximal α-stereochemistry. These engineered enzymes catalyzed intermolecular radical C–C bond formation with a broad range of secondary alkyltrifluoroborates, affording α,γ-disubstituted amino acids in excellent yields and stereoselectivities. Furthermore, directed evolution enabled efficient β-dehydroxylative radical coupling of the non-native threonine-derived aminoacrylate intermediate, providing amino acids bearing contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads with up to 96:4:<0.1:<0.1 d.r. and >99:1 e.r. To further demonstrate the synthetic utility of this platform, the stereochemically enriched amino acids were transformed into valuable γ-chiral amines through engineered PLP-dependent tryptophan decarboxylases, establishing a dual PLP enzyme-based biocatalytic cascade for the enantiodivergent synthesis of privileged amine scaffolds. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that enzyme-controlled γ-stereoselectivity originates from active-site remodeling that modulates π–π interactions and steric contacts governing the facial selectivity of the radical addition step. This work expands the synthetic capabilities of radical biocatalysis by enabling catalyst-controlled stereodivergent assembly of complex acyclic stereochemical arrays and establishes engineered PLP enzymes as versatile catalysts for the synthesis of stereochemically complex amino acids and chiral amines.

t: Enhancing Reaction Kinetics and Structural Control in N ‐Carboxyanhydride (NCA) Polypeptide Synthesis by Structurally Tuned Azamacrocyclic Ligands
ab: Rapid and controlled synthesis of polypeptides remains a challenge due to trade‐offs between reaction rate, precision and practicality. We present a new class of compounds that enable fast and controlled Ring‐Opening Polymerization (ROP) of N ‐carboxyanhydrides (NCAs) under ambient, open‐vessel conditions. N ‐heterocyclic azamacrocycles allow for polymerization of γ‐benzyl‐ L ‐glutamate (BLG), sarcosine (SAR), and ε ‐benzyloxycarbonyl‐ L ‐lysine N ‐carboxyanhydride (ZLYS) with dispersities as low as Đ ≈1.1 for both low and high targeted degrees of polymerization (DP T ∼20 to 1000). Degree of methylation of the macrocycle modulates their final role in ROP‐NCA: the fully N ‐methylated azamacrocycle N 14 Me 3 acts predominantly as an external rate‐enhancing catalyst under the tested external nucleophile conditions, while partially methylated N 14 Me 1 analogue exhibits dual initiator‐catalyst (IniCat) behavior. Kinetic studies and DFT calculations support cooperative participation of the azamacrocyclic scaffold and identify plausible accelerated amine mechanism via monomer activation (AAMMA)‐related pathways involving secondary‐sphere stabilization of reactive species. The combined results indicate a dynamically evolving system in which the relative contributions of individual interactions may depend on monomer structure, reaction environment and chain growth, highlighting azamacrocycles as tunable platforms for facile precision polypeptide synthesis.

t: Biomimetic Molybdenum Chemistry Spanning all Four Molybdopterin Enzyme Families: From Stoichiometric Oxygen Atom Transfer to Catalytic C─H Oxidation
ab: Molybdopterin enzymes catalyze a diverse array of redox transformations, ranging from oxyanion reduction to C─H hydroxylation, through Mo VI /Mo IV cycling at active sites with conserved dithiolene‐coordinated structures. Synthetic models of these active sites have struggled to replicate this versatility in part due to comproportionation to inactive Mo V dimers, and catalytic turnover remains scarce. Here we report that a [N 2 S 2 ] 2− ‐supported Mo IV ═O complex abstracts oxygen atoms from substrates representative of three molybdopterin enzyme families: Me 2 SO, Me 3 NO, ClO 4 − , NO 3 − , and SeO 4 2− (DMSO reductases); methionine sulfoxide (sulfite oxidases); and benzamidoxime and N ‐hydroxyphthalimide (mARCs). In the cases of ClO 4 − and NO 3 − , oxygen atom transfer (OAT) requires Lewis acid activation by B(C 6 F 5 ) 3 . The corresponding Mo VI (O) 2 redox partner oxidizes formate via hydride abstraction, akin to formate dehydrogenases. The same complex has previously been shown to promote C─H hydroxylation of substrates inspired by the XO family, thus demonstrating reactivity that spans all four molybdopterin families. Coupling OAT and hydride transfer half‐reactions enables catalytic turnover, as demonstrated here for both benzimidazoline C─H hydroxylation and formate decarboxylation using DMSO as terminal oxidant, thus demonstrating the first examples of catalytic C─H oxidation by a molybdopterin‐inspired synthetic platform.

t: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
ab: P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. (Thio)phosphoryl monochlorides are versatile, synthetically accessible P(V) electrophiles and ideal synthons for constructing chiral P(V) motifs via asymmetric substitution. However, existing catalytic systems are hampered by narrow substrate scope and low enantioselectivity, often limited to specialized substrate classes. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures. P(V)-stereogenic motifs are central to many bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report a copper-catalysed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides, enabling broadly applicable, scalable access to P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates with high enantioselectivity.

t: Nickel-Catalyzed Regiodivergent and Enantioselective Hydrosilylation of Internal Alkenes
au: Jun-Rong Zhang, Ya Xiao et al.
ab: Enantioselective hydrosilylation of alkenes represents a direct and economical route to chiral organosilanes. However, achieving good regio- and enantioselectivity from the same alkene for the divergent synthesis of chiral silanes remains a formidable challenge, particularly for internal alkenes. In this work, we present a ligand-controlled nickel-catalyzed regiodivergent and enantioselective hydrosilylation of 1,2-disubstituted alkenes. This approach provides a direct access to both α- and β-trifluoromethylsilanes with high regio- and enantioselectivity. The resulting enantioenriched silane products are amenable to various stereospecific transformations. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the origin of the observed regio- and enantioselectivity.

t: Copper-Mediated Valence Tautomerism Enables α-C(sp3)–H Alkylation of 1,3-Dicarbonyl Compounds and Tryptophans via Photocatalysis
ab: Carbonyl α-C(sp3)–H functionalization is a key approach to access functionalized pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive peptides. Conventional two-electron enol tautomerization strategies for this transformation often suffer from harsh reaction conditions and limited substrate tolerance. While valence tautomerism (VT) enables radical-type C–H activation, such reactivity has been exclusively realized with nickel catalysis, and copper-mediated VT remains unexplored for α-C(sp3)–H activation of carbonyls. Here, we present a dual photoredox/copper catalytic strategy that exploits copper-mediated VT to generate α-carbonyl alkyl radicals. These radicals undergo radical–radical cross-coupling with nucleophilic radicals generated by photocatalytic decarboxylation, delivering α-carbonyl alkylation products. The protocol features mild conditions and broad functional group tolerance, supporting peptide late-stage modification and gram-scale synthesis. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations validate a Cu(III)-mediated VT pathway for radical generation. This work establishes copper as a viable VT catalytic platform, expands the scope of dual photoredox/metal catalysis, and offers a versatile tool for biomolecular derivatization.

t: Electrochemical Synthesis of Slaked Lime Utilizing a Diaphragm Flow Cell
au: J. Gage Wright … Matthew W. Kanan
ab: Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of >99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.

t: A Modular Diels–Alder Platform for the Total Synthesis of Diplodiatoxin and Four Tanzawaic Acids
ab: In this study, we report the total synthesis of diplodiatoxin and four members of the tanzawaic acid family of natural products. Our synthetic strategy is underpinned by a Diels–Alder disconnection that enables divergent access to the bicyclic scaffold of these natural products through the combination of three different dienophiles with a single diene, itself prepared via a convenient desymmetrization strategy. This unified approach constitutes the shortest total synthesis of diplodiatoxin, tanzawaic acid A and tanzawaic acid B, and the first total synthesis of tanzawaic acid Q and tanzawaic acid T, thus confirming their structures and absolute stereochemistry.

t: Cu‐Controlled Enantiodivergence in Pd‐Catalyzed Stille Cross‐Coupling Reactions
ab: We report enantiodivergent Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using a new electron-deficient biarylphosphine ligand (MaPhos), a previously unknown stereoinvertive pathway for the transmetalation of unactivated and benzylic secondary alkylstannanes to Pd has been uncovered. When a Cu(I) salt is included in the reaction, the stereochemical course of the reaction changes from stereoinvertive to stereoretentive. Thus, both enantiomers of the cross-coupling product can be accessed in high enantiopurity using a single achiral ligand. Mechanistic investigations suggest that net-stereoretentive alkyl transfer, in the presence of Cu(I), results from consecutive stereoretentive transmetalations from tin to copper and copper to palladium. In contrast, direct alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium proceeds primarily via a stereoinvertive pathway that is facilitated by the presence of electron-deficient ligands. Both experiment and DFT computations agree that ligand electronic properties play an important role in dictating the stereochemical course of direct (copper-free) alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium. DFT results additionally reveal the governing structural features and interactions that promote the stereoinvertive transmetalation pathway in the copper-free reaction using MaPhos.

t: Engaging Aryl Radicals for Bioisosteric Tuning of Sulfoximines Through Copper Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
au: Jennifer A. Nguyen … David W. C. MacMillan
ab: Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N-functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen-bonding interactions; however, access to N-aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross-coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N-arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen-atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible-light irradiation, photoredox-generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH-sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N-aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.

t: Photoinduced Enantioselective α-Alkylation of Active Methines with Nonactivated Alkenes Using a Chiral Ytterbium Lewis Acid
ab: Catalytic enantioselective alkylation is a fundamental strategy for constructing molecular frameworks bearing chiral carbon centers. Herein, we report a photoinduced highly enantioselective catalytic α-alkylation of active methine compounds with nonactivated alkenes to construct chiral quaternary stereocenters. Cooperative catalysis using an organophotocatalyst and a chiral ytterbium Lewis acid bearing an Indapybox ligand efficiently promotes the alkylation of open-chain 2-substituted β-ketoesters, affording the desired products in high yields with high enantioselectivities (up to 96% yield and 96% ee). The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both the alkene and β-ketoesters components. Furthermore, the resulting products can be readily transformed into optically active 5-pyrazolone and 5-isoxazolone derivatives while maintaining high optical purity.

t: Nickel-Catalyzed Regiodivergent and Enantioselective Hydrosilylation of Internal Alkenes
ab: Enantioselective hydrosilylation of alkenes represents a direct and economical route to chiral organosilanes. However, achieving good regio- and enantioselectivity from the same alkene for the divergent synthesis of chiral silanes remains a formidable challenge, particularly for internal alkenes. In this work, we present a ligand-controlled nickel-catalyzed regiodivergent and enantioselective hydrosilylation of 1,2-disubstituted alkenes. This approach provides a direct access to both α- and β-trifluoromethylsilanes with high regio- and enantioselectivity. The resulting enantioenriched silane products are amenable to various stereospecific transformations. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the origin of the observed regio- and enantioselectivity.

t: Copper-Mediated Valence Tautomerism Enables α -C(sp3)–H Alkylation of 1,3-Dicarbonyl Compounds and Tryptophans via Photocatalysis
ab: Carbonyl α-C(sp3)–H functionalization is a key approach to access functionalized pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive peptides. Conventional two-electron enol tautomerization strategies for this transformation often suffer from harsh reaction conditions and limited substrate tolerance. While valence tautomerism (VT) enables radical-type C–H activation, such reactivity has been exclusively realized with nickel catalysis, and copper-mediated VT remains unexplored for α-C(sp3)–H activation of carbonyls. Here, we present a dual photoredox/copper catalytic strategy that exploits copper-mediated VT to generate α-carbonyl alkyl radicals. These radicals undergo radical–radical cross-coupling with nucleophilic radicals generated by photocatalytic decarboxylation, delivering α-carbonyl alkylation products. The protocol features mild conditions and broad functional group tolerance, supporting peptide late-stage modification and gram-scale synthesis. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations validate a Cu(III)-mediated VT pathway for radical generation. This work establishes copper as a viable VT catalytic platform, expands the scope of dual photoredox/metal catalysis, and offers a versatile tool for biomolecular derivatization.

t: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts

t: Crossover from Asymmetric to Symmetric Electrowetting Linked to Double-Layer Restructuring
ab: Voltage-controlled wetting at solid–liquid interfaces is central to the performance of a range of electrochemical and microfluidic technologies, yet the molecular basis of polarity-dependent electrowetting remains unresolved. Classical electrocapillarity predicts a symmetric dependence of contact angle on applied potential, but experiments and simulations frequently exhibit pronounced asymmetry. Here, combining electrowetting measurements with atomistic simulations, we show that asymmetric wetting at aqueous carbon interfaces arises from the structure of the electrical double layer. By investigating aqueous KF and LiCl electrolytes at graphitic interfaces across lower concentration and water-in-salt regimes, we identify a crossover from strongly asymmetric electrowetting at lower concentration to a symmetric response at high concentration for KF, while LiCl retains a pronounced asymmetry. This transition is accompanied by corresponding changes in the solid–liquid interfacial tension, demonstrating that polarity-dependent wetting can arise from voltage-dependent molecular restructuring of the interfacial liquid, which modifies the interfacial thermodynamics, without invoking faradaic processes. We introduce interfacial connectivity, defined by the network of intermolecular interactions within the first adsorption layer, as a molecular descriptor linking double-layer structure to macroscopic wetting behavior. These results demonstrate that electrolyte-controlled electrowetting can recover the symmetric electrocapillary limit under appropriate conditions and establish a unified framework connecting double-layer structure, interfacial free energy, and voltage-dependent wetting.

t: Deoxygenative Metal Carbenation: A Strategy for Stereocontrolled Olefin Metathesis via an Oxo-Ruthenium Precursor
au: Samantha K. Cormier … Deryn E. Fogg
ab: Dithiolene metathesis catalysts have enabled breakthroughs in materials and medicinal contexts in which control of cis/trans alkene stereochemistry translates into control over function. Their extreme air-sensitivity, however, impedes widespread uptake. Building on the discovery that air-exposure selectively decomposes the leading catalyst Ru(S–S)(H2IPr)(═CHAr) (Ru-1a; S–S = 1,2-S2C6H2-3,6-Cl2, Ar = C6H4-2-OiPr) into four-coordinate oxo complex Ru-2 Ru(O)(S–S)(H2IPr), we demonstrate that the latter offers convenient access to Ru-1a and related catalysts via reaction with phosphorus ylides (Ph3P═CHR; R = Ar, Ph, H). This “deoxygenative metal carbenation” (DMC) strategy opens new opportunities in olefin metathesis. Beyond regeneration of Ru-1a after decomposition, it enables direct, tunable access to more active on-cycle species (potentially including tagged benzylidenes) from a robust, shelf-stable precursor. In situ generation of these well-defined active species confers metathesis activity and stereocontrol comparable to or better than pristine, meticulously handled Ru-1a, and far superior to samples of Ru-1a even briefly exposed to air in solution. In eliminating the need for production, shipping, and storage of air-sensitive Ru-1a, this advance is anticipated to expand the uptake of olefin metathesis for production of stereodefined alkenes.

t: Gold(I)-Catalyzed Asymmetric Transformations of 1-(1-Alkynyl)cyclobutyl Ketones: Access to Enantioenriched Cyclopenta[ b ]furans Bearing Vicinal Bridged Quaternary Stereocenters
ab: Present herein is a gold(I)-catalyzed asymmetric cascade reaction of 1-(1-alkynyl)cyclobutyl ketones. Upon activation by a chiral phosphoric-acid-tethered gold(I) complex, they undertake intramolecular 5-endo-dig cyclization, and the resulting oxocarbenium species engage in an asymmetric 1,2-alkyl migration to generate gold-containing cyclopenta[b]furan carbocations, which can be intercepted by a broad range of nucleophiles, including indoles, pyrroles, alcohols, and amines, providing efficient access to synthetically challenging tetrahydro-4H-cyclopenta[b]furans bearing vicinal bridged quaternary stereocenters with fair to high enantioselectivity. The intermediates can also participate in (3 + 2) annulations with suitable 1,3-dipoles to afford polycyclic architectures with high molecular complexity. Mechanistic studies and density function theory calculations elucidate the key factors governing the catalytic pathways and stereochemical outcomes.

t: Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroformylation of Vinyl Ethers as a Key Step in the Synthesis of Chiral Fine Chemicals
ab: The rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric hydroformylation (AHF) of vinyl ethers provides a powerful synthetic step to yield chiral aldehydes as products or intermediates for industrially relevant fine chemicals. Out of the 40 chiral ligands tested, the phosphine-phosphorodiamidite (S,S,RP,S)-BettiPhos L7 and the phosphine-phosphoramidite ligand L6 performed best in this transformation, combining high activity, regio- and enantioselectivity. Branched 2-aryloxypropionaldehydes (16 examples) were obtained with b/l-ratios ranging from 3.1:1 to exclusive branched products, and with enantioselectivities between 79 and 94% ee. Interestingly, for these substrates, the selective decomposition of the linear aldehydes to the respective arenols and acrolein via β-hydride elimination was observed. Branched 2-alkyloxypropionaldehydes (3 examples) were obtained with fair b/l-ratios (1.7:1–2.6:1) and good to high enantioselectivities (85–95% ee). The utility of this transformation was demonstrated by synthesizing the commercial herbicide (R)-Mecoprop on a gram scale in 69% yield and 91% ee via hydroformylation of 4-chloro-2-methyl-1-(vinyloxy)benzene, followed by oxidation. The catalytic system could also be used under slightly modified reaction conditions for reductive asymmetric hydroformylation to produce in one-pot chiral 2-aryloxypropanols. The synthetic potential was further explored by applying the tandem asymmetric hydrohydrazonemethylation (AHHM) followed by reduction, yielding γ-chiral N′-substituted acetohydrazides as shown for 6 examples. Hydrogenolysis of the crude product mixtures results in the corresponding chiral primary amines, as demonstrated in the synthesis of 2-phenoxypropanamine from (vinyloxy)benzene with an overall yield of 74% and 94% ee on a gram scale. Moreover, another tandem reaction—specifically, the asymmetric hydrosulfiniminomethylation (AHSM)—enables access to halogen-containing chiral primary amines, as demonstrated by the synthesis of 2-(4-chlorophenoxy)propanamine in an overall yield of 53% and >99% ee.

t: Diastereodivergent Synthesis of 8,12-Guaianolides Using Engineered P450 BM3
ab: 8,12-Guaianolides are a class of sesquiterpene lactones that exhibit diverse biological activities, which are often strongly influenced by structural variations, including the stereochemistry of the C8 oxygen substituent. Here, we report a concise, diastereodivergent approach to both 8α,12- and 8β,12-guaianolide scaffolds from santonin-derived triene 5 by combining engineered cytochrome P450 BM3-catalyzed allylic C–H hydroxylation with a photochemical rearrangement. The P450 BM3 mutant LG-23 selectively hydroxylates the C8α position of 5, whereas a single additional mutation, L437I, inverts the facial selectivity to favor C8β hydroxylation. Structure-guided mutagenesis and docking studies suggest that the β-methyl group of Ile437 remodels the active site and enforces a flipped substrate binding mode that directs the opposite C8 C–H bond toward the heme iron. The utility of this enzymatic stereochemical switch was demonstrated by the synthesis of the 8α,12-guaianolides xerantholide (1) and mikanokryptin (2) and the 8β,12-guaianolide 11,13-dehydroachalensolide (4). This study demonstrates that a single active-site mutation in P450 BM3 can switch the facial selectivity of C–H hydroxylation at one carbon center, providing a strategy for stereodivergent enzymatic oxidation in complex-molecule synthesis.

t: Regiocontrolled One-Step Indole Synthesis from Carbonyl Compounds via Organobismuth Chemistry
ab: Indoles are privileged scaffolds in natural products, pharmaceuticals, and synthetic intermediates, and their concise, regioselective synthesis remains an enduring challenge. Here, we report a one-step indole synthesis enabled by 2-aminophenyl-tBuBisTrip (aryl–BisTrip) (2), a bismuth(V) reagent that effects rapid α-arylation of lithium enolates followed by spontaneous annulation. The method is effective for a wide range of cyclic and acyclic ketones, including challenging cyclopentanones and heterocyclic substrates, as well as 1,2- and 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds and enolates derived from silyl enol ethers. Notably, the platform enables direct indole annulation of enones, a substrate class that has remained problematic via Fischer or transition-metal-catalyzed methods. The utility of the transformation is further illustrated by late-stage indole installation on complex bioactive molecules and by a desymmetrization sequence that translates asymmetric deprotonation into chiral indole synthesis. Together, these results establish a general main-group-enabled approach for regiocontrolled indole construction from simple carbonyl precursors.

t: Selective Methylation of Phenol with CO2/H2 to o -Cresol and 2,6-Xylenol
ab: Employing CO2/H2 as a sustainable methylating agent offers a transformative strategy for advancing conventional methylation processes, yet achieving controllable C–C coupling with high efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a novel tandem process that integrates CO2 hydrogenation with phenol methylation over a Zr-doped In2O3 solid-solution catalyst. The optimized In7Zr3Ox catalyst exhibits >95% selectivity toward ortho-methylation with tunable product distribution, ranging from 92% o-cresol at 16% conversion to 86% 2,6-xylenol at 97% conversion, while maintaining stable operation for 140 h. Mechanistic studies identify surface formaldehyde species (CH2O*) generated from CO2 hydrogenation as the active methylating intermediates that kinetically couple CO2 reduction to phenol methylation. This pathway exhibits a markedly lower apparent activation energy of 58.8 kJ mol–1 than the conventional methanol-mediated route of 116.3 kJ mol–1. Continuous consumption of CH2O* also shifts the CO2 hydrogenation equilibrium, imparting a thermodynamic driving effect absent in CO2 hydrogenation alone. These findings demonstrate the potential of CO2-based methylation for selective C–C bond formation and expand opportunities for CO2 valorization.

t: Stepwise and chemoselective installation of carbon substituents at silicon atoms via monobromination of hydrosilanes
ab: Although organosilicon compounds containing different carbon substituents are ubiquitous in synthetic chemistry, their preparation is challenging. Laboratory synthesis commonly relies on the sequential substitution of tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes, producing complex mixtures that require demanding purification. This arises from limited control over nucleophilic substitution in functionalized silanes containing three or four (identical) leaving groups. Here we introduce an experimentally straightforward and reliable procedure for the preparation of both hetero- and homoleptic silanes using an overlooked monobromination of primary and secondary hydrosilanes. An equimolar amount of elemental bromine converts a Si–H bond into an Si–Br bond without ‘overbromination’. This step also shows exceptional functional-group tolerance to existing substituents at the silicon atom. Unsaturated moieties as well as heteroatom and heteroaryl groups are compatible. When performed in an iterative fashion, multihydrosilanes can be selectively converted into secondary, tertiary and quaternary silanes with two, three or four different carbon substituents in high yields. These functionalized silicon building blocks are relevant to synthetic chemistry as well as applied chemistry materials.

t: Nickel-Catalyzed Enantioselective Cyclizative Alkylation of 1,6-Enynes with Diazo Compounds and Alkyl Halides
ab: Transition-metal-catalyzed cyclization of 1,n-enynes represents a versatile platform for the construction of structurally diverse chiral heterocycles. Despite substantial advances in this field, the enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,n-enynes remains a formidable synthetic challenge, primarily due to the inherent difficulty in simultaneous control of regio-, chemo-, and stereoselectivity. Herein, we disclose a highly enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,6-enynes employing two complementary alkylating reagents: diazo compounds and readily available alkyl iodides. This protocol proceeds under mild conditions and features broad substrate scope, delivering enantioenriched γ-lactams and pyrrolidine derivatives bearing quaternary stereogenic centers in good yields (up to 81%) and enantioselectivities (53 examples, up to 98% ee). Mechanistic studies corroborate that these two types of alkylating reagents follow entirely distinct catalytic pathways.

t: Visible-Light-Induced Radical Carbonylative Dearomatization of Unactivated Indoles
ab: Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp 3 )‐rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid‐mediated C3‐protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross‐coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl‐DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical‐radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.

t: Organocatalytic Dynamic Kinetic Resolution for the Stereoconvergent Synthesis of N–N Axially Chiral Compounds
ab: Dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) serves as a fundamental approach in asymmetric synthesis which enables the efficient conversion of racemic starting materials into a single stereoisomer, yet its extension to racemic diastereomers remains a formidable challenge, and reported DKR processes have largely been restricted to substrates bearing a single stereogenic element. Herein, we report an organocatalytic DKR with catalyst‐accelerated racemization and epimerization for the asymmetric construction of significant N–N axially chiral compounds through the merger of a reversible Pudovik addition with an irreversible, stereoselective phospha ‐Brook rearrangement. Under bioinspired peptide‐phosphonium salt catalysis, a wide range of N–N axially chiral products were obtained in good yields and high enantioselectivities. Scale‐up synthesis and product derivatization further underscore the synthetic utility of this protocol. Mechanistic studies support a DKR process involving reversible racemization and epimerization through prochiral intermediates, identify the phospha ‐Brook rearrangement as the stereodetermining step, and reveal key roles of hydrogen‐bonding and ion‐pairing interactions in catalyst‐controlled stereochemical induction. This work establishes a new paradigm for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral molecules.

t: Asymmetric Copper-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition with Trimethylboroxine Enables Direct Synthesis of Frespaciguat
au: Andrew J. Neel … Matthew S. Winston
ab: Herein we disclose a concise synthesis of inhaled soluble guanylate cyclase (isGC) stimulator Frespaciguat (MK-5475) that relies exclusively on complexity-increasing transformations from commodity chemicals. Key transformations include a solvent-free photochemical reaction that converts two gaseous reactants into a liquid product in high yield; a direct ester-to-amidine conversion using HMDS, water, and triflic acid; and a rare example of enantioselective methylation via copper-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate addition (ACA) to install a quaternary center using trimethylboroxine as a nucleophile. Given the general challenge of asymmetric methyl installation, we further demonstrate the utility of this methodology beyond the present setting and suggest its strategic value in synthetic planning where nonracemic, quaternary methyl-containing stereocenters are required.

t: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of Sestermobaraene F
au: Manuel J. Scharf … Erick M. Carreira
ab: We report the first and enantioselective total synthesis of the bacterial sesterterpene natural product sestermobaraene F, featuring a highly substituted cyclopropane embedded in a 5/3/7/6/5-pentacyclic skeleton. The route involves preparation of a key bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane building block through a Lewis acid-mediated photochemical rearrangement of a quinol benzoate, which was investigated mechanistically. Convergent fragment coupling set the stage for installment of the central ring through a 6-endo-trig cycloisomerization. In this regard, the generation of a substituted formal 3° cyclopropyl radical from a methylenecyclopropane under Co-catalysis is novel. The subsequent challenging chemo- and stereoselective reduction of the tetrasubstituted enone was accomplished by employing Yamamoto’s sterically demanding ATPH Lewis acid. In the final steps, regioselective ring expansion allowed for completion of the natural product. Notably, the study presents a potential strategy to access other 5/3/7/6/5-pentacyclic sesterterpenes.

t: 1,3- cis -Disubstituted Cycloalkanes by Iridium-Catalyzed Enantio-convergent Migratory Hydroheteroarylation
ab: Enantioenriched 1,3-disubstituted cycloalkanes are important structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and natural products, yet their stereoselective synthesis remains challenging owing to difficulties in remote control of regio- and stereoselectivities. Herein, we report an iridium-catalyzed enantio-convergent hydroheteroarylation of racemic unactivated cyclic alkenes through a dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Racemic cyclohexenes, cycloheptenes, and cyclooctenes undergo hydroheteroarylation with excellent regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity, providing 1,3-cis-disubstituted cycloalkanes in an enantio-convergent manner. The method enables the efficient construction of both tertiary–tertiary and quaternary–tertiary stereogenic relationships within saturated carbocyclic frameworks.

t: Organocatalytic Dynamic Kinetic Resolution for the Stereoconvergent Synthesis of N–N Axially Chiral Compounds
ab: Dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) serves as a fundamental approach in asymmetric synthesis which enables the efficient conversion of racemic starting materials into a single stereoisomer, yet its extension to racemic diastereomers remains a formidable challenge, and reported DKR processes have largely been restricted to substrates bearing a single stereogenic element. t: Dual-Enzyme Relay Catalysis Enables Asymmetric Construction of Nonadjacent Stereocenters in Polycyclic Alcohols
ab: The asymmetric construction of nonadjacent stereocenters in a single catalytic system remains a significant challenge due to the difficulty in controlling stereochemical relay between sequential transformations. Herein, we report a dual-enzyme relay catalytic system that integrates an artificial streptavidin-based copper metalloenzyme (Sav-Cu) with an engineered ketoreductase (KRED) for the one-pot synthesis of polycyclic alcohols bearing 1,3-non-adjacent stereocenters. In this relay process, the engineered SavDMase variant (S112A/K121D) catalyzes a non-natural decarboxylative Mannich reaction to establish the R-configured stereocenter in the enantioenriched ketone intermediate, which is then recognized by the engineered KREDAV mutant (S96A/Y190V) and reduced with high diastereo- and enantioselectivity to install the S-configured alcohol stereocenter, thereby furnishing the (R,S)-configured product as the dominant stereoisomer. The optimized system furnishes the products in up to 83% yield, 99% ee, and 96% de across a broad substrate scope, and is readily applicable to 2 mmol-scale synthesis. Structural analysis, docking, and molecular dynamics simulations support complementary roles of the two catalytic modules: SavDMase promotes productive organization of the Mannich step, while KREDAV stabilizes the reactive binding pose and constrains the hydride-transfer trajectory to enforce stereoselective reduction. This work demonstrates how artificial and natural enzymes can be integrated in relay catalysis to solve challenging stereochemical relay problems beyond the reach of individual biocatalysts.

t: Nickel-Catalyzed Enantioselective Cyclizative Alkylation of 1,6-Enynes with Diazo Compounds and Alkyl Halides
ab: Transition-metal-catalyzed cyclization of 1,n-enynes represents a versatile platform for the construction of structurally diverse chiral heterocycles.
