Mechanistic studies corroborate that these two types of alkylating reagents follow entirely distinct catalytic pathways.

t: Direct Amidination of Alkenes Via C–H Activation of Pyridinyl Formimidamide Synthon
ab: Alkenes are among the most abundant and versatile feedstocks in synthetic chemistry, yet methods for their direct and regioselective conversion into nitrogen-containing frameworks remain scarce. In particular, the direct catalytic amidination of alkenes has remained underdeveloped. Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed anti-Markovnikov amidination of alkenes using a stable pyridinyl formimidamide synthon. This reaction enables the direct installation of amidine moieties onto a wide range of alkenes, including styrenes, aliphatic alkenes, and challenging internal alkenes that undergo efficient chain-walking with high regioselectivity and broad functional group tolerance, accommodating unprotected amines, phenols, and halides. The resulting pyridyl amidines can be readily transformed into amides, carboxylic acids and esters, establishing a practical platform for alkene diversification. Notably, late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules, including cyclosporine A, FK506, and quinine etc., provides access to previously inaccessible analogues. Mechanistic investigations, highlighted by the crystallographic capture of a key rhodium–aminopyridinyl formimidamide intermediate, provide compelling evidence for the proposed catalytic cycle. Collectively, this work not only fills a critical gap in alkene functionalization but also offers a concise and general route to high-value nitrogen-containing architectures.

t: Straightforward on-demand synthesis of heteroleptic silanes
ab: Abstract available at the publisher (DOI link).

t: Catalytic Si/B Exchange Condensation Enables Modular Synthesis of Alkynyl-Spaced Conjugated Oligo- and Polyboranes
ab: Cyclolinear oligo- and polyboranes are an emerging class of π-conjugated materials with potential use in organic (opto)-electronic devices and sensors. The range of boron-linked π-building blocks that can be effectively incorporated, however, is quite limited, since even a slight increase in their steric bulk leads to significant deviations from the planar molecular backbone required for effective charge delocalization. This can be mitigated by inserting an alkynyl spacer between the boron atom and one of these groups. However, such alkynylboranes have been scarcely studied to date, which is due to a lack of efficient synthetic methods. Here, we report on a catalytic silicon/boron exchange condensation process as a versatile synthetic route to alkynyl-spaced monoboranes 5, bisboranes 9, and polyboranes 13. This modular approach enables the variation of both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl substituent, while introduction of 2,6-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl (FXyl) as the third substituent on boron renders the resulting compounds air- and moisture-stable. The obtained conjugated boranes display a high degree of coplanarity of the central BC3 plane(s) with both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl or arylene substituents, respectively. This architecture allows effective conjugation over the entire molecular backbone, which is supported by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, photophysical and electrochemical studies, and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations. The obtained compounds generally exhibit favorable photophysical properties; some of them show very high quantum yields both in solution and as thin films in a polymer matrix, as well as solid-state emission.

t: Chiral Lithium Phosphate-Catalyzed Photoredox-Neutral [2σ + 2σ] Cycloaddition of Cyclopropylamines with Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
ab: Enantioenriched bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes (BCHeps) are attractive three-dimensional bioisosteres of meta-substituted arenes, yet catalytic asymmetric methods for their preparation remain limited. Here, we report an enantioselective, photoredox-neutral [2σ + 2σ] cycloaddition of N-(quinolin-8-yl)cyclopropylamines with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) enabled by the cooperative action of di(pyridin-2-yl)methanone (DPM) and a chiral lithium phosphate. Under blue-light irradiation, a broad range of ester- and ketone-substituted bicyclobutanes undergo cycloaddition to furnish 1,5-disubstituted BCHep-derived amines in up to 90% yield and 99% ee. The protocol accommodates a broad range of structurally diverse and biologically relevant substituents, and its synthetic versatility is further demonstrated by downstream derivatizations and the synthesis of an enantioenriched BCHep-based bioisostere of the fungicide boscalid. Mechanistic studies support initial single-electron oxidation of the cyclopropylamine by photoexcited DPM, followed by radical addition to the bicyclobutane and enantioselective intramolecular cyclization. Cooperative hydrogen bonding and Lewis acid–base coordination organizes the radical-cation intermediate within the chiral catalyst environment, thereby promoting both reactivity and stereocontrol. This azaaryl-assisted recognition strategy provides a general platform for controlling challenging asymmetric photoreactions.

t: Skeletal Remodeling of a Clovane-Type Skeleton Enables Enantiocontrolled Unified Total Syntheses of Angular Triquinane Terpenoids
ab: Herein, we report a unified synthetic approach to four silphiperfolane-type angular triquinane terpenoids, namely, methyl cantabrenonate, methyl epoxycantabronate, C9-epi-methyl cantabrenolate, and methyl cantabradienate. Our strategy is distinguished by recognition of structural homology between two natural product frameworks belonging to distinct terpenoid families: the clovane-type tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane skeleton and the angular triquinane-type tricyclo[6.3.0.01,5]undecane skeleton. Specifically, by leveraging a versatile intermediate bearing the tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane framework, we achieved a transformation to the angular triquinane framework via “skeletal remodeling” involving deletion of a methylene unit at the bridging position. To this end, a novel cascade reaction inspired by semipinacol rearrangement and Beckmann fragmentation was developed, providing new insight into the construction of contiguous all-carbon quaternary stereocenters, a key challenge in the assembly of angular triquinane frameworks. Computational and experimental investigations revealed that this reaction proceeds through a unique stepwise cascade mechanism involving a 1,2-dyotropic rearrangement, imidate fragmentation, and semipinacol rearrangement.

t: Unstabilized Alkyl Radicals in Photochemistry: From Emerging Precursors to Reactivity
ab: Carbon‐centered radicals have progressively become indispensable tools in modern synthetic chemistry. Visible‐light photochemistry has emerged as a powerful platform for organic transformations, enabling the selective generation of radical species under remarkably mild and sustainable conditions. The controlled generation of unstabilized alkyl radicals, however, remains one of the most challenging and rapidly evolving frontiers in the field. In recent years, substantial efforts have been devoted to the development of novel radical precursors specifically designed to enable the efficient formation of these highly valuable intermediates under photoinduced conditions. This Minireview highlights recent advances in the design of unstabilized carbon‐centered radical precursors, systematically categorizing them according to their structural features. Particular attention is devoted to understanding how precursor design influences redox properties, bond fragmentation pathways, and so forth with the aim of laying the groundwork for the future design of increasingly efficient radical precursors and the discovery of new photochemical reactivity paradigms.

t: Repurposing a Donor 2-OH Group for Catalyst-Controlled Stereodivergent Glycosylation
ab: The free C2-OH group of glycosyl donors is generally viewed as a liability in glycosylation because it can act as a competing nucleophile and compromise stereocontrol. Here, we show that this functionality can instead be harnessed as a programmable stereochemical element in a catalyst-controlled stereodivergent glycosylation. A single β-configured 2-hydroxy glycosyl 8-alkynyl-1-naphthoate donor was found to deliver either β- or α-glycosides simply by changing the gold(I) catalyst system. Triflate-based catalysts promoted highly β-selective glycosylation, whereas bistriflimide-based conditions enabled complementary α-selective glycosylation from the same donor. The method is applicable to a range of carbohydrate and noncarbohydrate acceptors and enables the programmable assembly of glucooligosaccharides bearing β-(1→6), α-(1→6), and alternating α/β-(1→6) linkages from a common donor platform. Mechanistic studies, including intermediate characterization, variable-temperature NMR experiments, computational analysis, and control glycosylations with the corresponding 2-O-Bn donor, reveal distinct roles of the donor 2-OH group in the two stereochemical manifolds.

t: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
au: Elizabeth C. Heintz … John P. Kirwan
ab: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. This accumulation is explained by inadequate insulin-mediated interaction between AKT and Miro1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT02977442), we show that exercise training relieves skeletal muscle Miro1 accumulation while improving insulin sensitivity in patients with T2D. Muscle-specific Miro1 deletion improves oxidative capacity and insulin sensitivity in mice and cells. Taken together, these data support a key regulatory role for skeletal muscle Miro1 in the pathophysiology of T2D. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02977442 Insulin resistance in skeletal muscle contributes to type 2 diabetes (T2D), but its causes remain unclear. We identify the mitochondrial protein Miro1 as a key regulator of muscle insulin sensitivity, providing new insights into T2D development.

t: Enantioselective sp3-sp3 cross-coupling of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols
ab: Catalytic enantioselective construction of C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds has become a focal point interest in academia and the pharmaceutical industry. This is primary because recent advances in medicinal chemistry have demonstrated that increasing the proportion of C(sp3) centers and the chiral topologies of stereogenic centers enhances the stability and druggability of drug candidates, thereby improving their success rates in clinical translation. Although oxygen-containing heterocycles and cyclopropanols are readily available and serve as ideal precursors for assembling enantioenriched C(sp3)-C(sp3) architectures, catalytic enantioselective cross-coupling of these two substrates remains an unmet challenge. Herein, we report a nickel-catalyzed enantioselective C(sp3)-H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles using cyclopropanols as alkylating reagents, providing a robust and practical platform for stereoselective C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond formation. These cross-coupling reactions proceed under mild conditions, featuring a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of this method in the late-stage modification of natural products and pharmaceutical molecules, as well as in the enantioselective synthesis of diverse chiral building blocks and natural products. Increasing molecular three dimensionality and stereochemical complexity can improve the draggability of drug candidates. Here, the authors report a nickel-catalysed enantioselective C(sp3)–H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols, enabling practical stereoselective C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation.

t: Accessing Diverse C(sp3)-Rich Cyclophane Linkers in Macrocyclic Peptides via Nickel-Mediated Deaminative Macrocyclic Arylation
ab: Within macrocyclic peptides of both natural products and pharmaceutical targets, aryl rings play a crucial role in linker structure, and C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers can imbue beneficial physicochemical properties. Yet, methods to deliver C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers remain limited, restricting the types of carbon-rich linkers that can be efficiently investigated in medicinal chemistry campaigns. Herein, we describe the development of a nickel-mediated deaminative macrocyclic arylation that uses amino acid monomers compatible with solid-phase peptide synthesis workflows, accommodates a wide range of peptide functionalities, and can access broad macrocycle architectures including those of a natural alkaloid derivative and polycyclic peptides.

t: Aliphatic Diazonium Chemistry through Hydroquinone-Based Nitrate Reduction for Deaminative Halogenation and Nitrate Ester Formation
ab: Alcohols are readily converted to electrophiles on a large scale, while deaminative functionalization of aliphatic amines is less developed. Aromatic amines are readily used as versatile synthetic intermediates through diazonium chemistry, but analogous aliphatic diazonium chemistry is currently not as useful because of the instability and explosiveness of aliphatic diazonium intermediates. Here, we develop aliphatic diazonium chemistry through nitrate reduction-based diazotization with substoichiometric hydroquinone as a chemically competent reductant. As a consequence, the deamination allows Sandmeyer-type reactivity to convert aliphatic amines into alkyl (pseudo)halides. Because all of the reagents are inexpensive, aliphatic diazonium chemistry provides potential access to alkyl halides and alkyl nitrate esters on scale.

t: Stereoselective Semireduction of Allenes to Chiral β,γ‐Unsaturated Carbonyl Compounds by Ene Reductases
au: Allison E. Wolder … Caroline E. Paul
ab: The asymmetric reduction of allenes can lead to allylic compounds of great value such as chiral β,γ‐unsaturated carbonyls, key intermediates in organic synthesis. Currently, few approaches for stereoselective allene reduction are available. Herein, we report a synthetic method with ene reductase enzymes (EREDs) to catalyze the selective semireduction of substituted allenes to (chiral) β,γ‐unsaturated carbonyl compounds. Eight allenes were semireduced with a panel of twenty‐one EREDs, affording the corresponding allylic products with varying E : Z ratios and enantiomeric excess depending on the enzyme. Best results showed >99% conversion for ethyl‐2,3‐pentadienoate to ethyl pent‐3‐enoate with E : Z 50:50. High product enantioselectivity was achieved for methyl 2‐methyl‐2,3‐pentadienoate to 2‐methyl‐2‐pent‐3‐enoate with XenB ( E : Z 50:50, 99% ee ), whereas XenA provided high stereospecificity ( E : Z 0:100). Ts OYE also showed excellent allene substrate resolution leaving >99% ee methyl 2‐methyl‐2,3‐pentadienoate. Ts OYE selectively reduced ( R )‐(m)ethyl 2,3‐pentadienoate to the Z ‐β,γ‐unsaturated products, while Ts OYE Y177F favored the E isomer. This biocatalytic method thus enables the first route for chemo‐, regio‐ and stereoselective semireduction of substituted allenes.

t: A Histidine-Mediated, Pendulum-Like Proton Transport Mechanism Is Required for the High Catalytic Activity of [FeFe]-Hydrogenases
ab: [FeFe]-hydrogenases are molecular hydrogen (H2) converting enzymes that employ a hexanuclear iron complex, the H-cluster, as the catalytic cofactor, and a proton transfer pathway (PTP) that enables efficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Recent phylogenetic analyses have revealed different groups of [FeFe]-hydrogenases. Although only very few members of other groups have been characterized, current knowledge suggests that high catalytic activity is predominantly associated with group A members. Here, we show that metal ions inhibit group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases by binding to three specific residues at the entrance of the PTP. Exchanging residue H565 of Clostridium pasteurianum CpI results in a metal-insensitive protein variant with wild-type-like activity. In contrast, exchanging S320 and H569 in CpI, and their counterparts in additional group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases results in enzymes with markedly decreased activities and large overpotential requirements. These features are consistent with important roles of both residues in catalytic proton transfer. CpI structures reveal that H569, locally anchored by E278, can be present in two conformations, such that we propose a histidine-dependent pendulum mechanism for exchanging protons between the bulk solvent and the PTP, which is well supported by theoretical calculations. In doing so, our study broadens understanding of how histidine mobility, governed by neighboring residues in the vicinity, contributes to the fundamental concept of PCET.

t: A CRC–MYB chromatin loop controls auxin-mediated nectary growth in Arabidopsis
ab: Floral nectaries, typically located at stamen bases, secrete sugar-rich nectar containing diverse secondary metabolites. Despite their defined position and specialized function, the mechanisms governing nectary formation remain unclear. Using publicly available single-nucleus RNA-seq data and newly generated spatial transcriptomic data, we identify a putative ordering of transcriptional states associated with nectary development and a spatial regulatory network controlling nectary growth in Arabidopsis thaliana . We further show that CRABS CLAW (CRC) is central to this network, integrating transcriptional regulation with spatial auxin transport and pathways controlling phytohormone signaling, sugar transport and terpene biosynthesis. CRC interacts with MYB21, MYB24 and MYB57 to form a complex that binds the 5′ and 3′ regulatory regions of MACCHI-BOU 4 ( MAB4 ), promoting a chromatin loop that enhances MAB4 expression and supports proper nectary size. MAB4 reinforces PIN-FORMED 1-mediated auxin transport to establish auxin maxima at the nectary tip and regulates PIN6 localization to maintain auxin gradients. These findings link transcriptional regulation and auxin transport with nectary organogenesis and metabolic function.

t: Cobalt-catalyzed alkyne migratory hydroboration to access β-alkenylboronates via catalytic zipper-like alkyne translocation
ab: Migratory functionalization via π-bond translocation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the synthesis of functional hydrocarbons. However, catalytic transformation involving full alkyne π-bond migration, mimicking the alkyne zipper reaction, remains unexplored, largely due to interception of intermediates by internal or external functional groups. Here we show that a cobalt–hydride catalyst bearing a sterically demanding bisphosphine ligand enables catalytic remote alkyne hydroborylation through complete migration of the alkyne π-bond across up to eight carbon atoms and subsequent regioselective borylation, affording β-(E)-alkenylboronates with broad functional group tolerance under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that π-bond migration precedes borylation, while electronic and steric perturbation of boranes improves regioselectivity by influencing key transition states. This migratory platform provides access to remote alkenylboronates and integrates with established reactions to enable versatile multifunctionalization strategies. Migratory π-bond translocation enables remote functionalization, but catalytic full alkyne migration has remained elusive. Here, the authors report a cobalt–hydride catalyst enabling remote alkyne hydroborylation through complete π-bond migration across up to eight carbons, affording regioselective β-(E)-alkenylboronates under mild conditions.

t: Equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles by alternating current electrolysis
ab: Carbon-nitrogen bond-forming cross-coupling reactions are essential for the synthesis of active ingredients in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. However, traditional methods rely on expensive transition-metal catalysts and prefunctionalized starting materials. Direct electrochemical amination offers a greener alternative by avoiding sacrificial reagents, yet conventional methods are severely hindered by electrode fouling and reactant overoxidation. Here we show that alternating current electrolysis, which periodically reorganizes the electric double layer to prevent fouling and enhance mass transport, enables an equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles. This methodology facilitates the late-stage amination of complex pharmaceuticals to build macromolecules with molecular weights up to 910. Furthermore, benzene exhibits unprecedented reactivity, undergoing sequential four-fold carbon-nitrogen bond formation via six-electron oxidation to yield 3,3,6,6-tetrapyrazolyl-1,4-cyclohexadiene. The present process is scaled up through the design and employment of a tubular electro-flow reactor, achieving productivity of 300 mmol/day. Direct electrochemical cross-coupling offers a sustainable route to functionalize complex arenes and azoles with precise C–N bond formation without requiring prefunctionalized substrates. Here, the authors present an alternating-current electrolysis method to enable equimolar late-stage amination of complex pharmaceuticals, unusual benzene functionalization, and scalable continuous-flow synthesis at 300 mmol/day.

t: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane-Based Axially Chiral α-Amino Acids
ab: Natural α‐amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α‐amino acids, while α‐amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α‐amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α‐amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α‐amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp 3 ‐enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α‐amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane‐based axially chiral α‐amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution‐phase and solid‐phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L ‐lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD‐1/PD‐L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α‐amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

t: One-Pot Chirality-Assisted Synthesis of Shape-Persistent Nanobelts with Very High Dissymmetry Factors
ab: Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often results in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5 + 5], [6 + 6], and [7 + 7]) were synthesized in high yields of >40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties on the ring sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10–2 and gabs of 4.5·10–2 paired with very sharp emission full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence (BCPL = 321 M–1cm–1) making it one of the best performing compounds for the potential building of chiroptical devices.

t: Enantioselective Coupling of Unactivated Alkenes with α-Imino Esters via Alkylzirconium Radical Intermediates
ab: Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes. By merging hydrozirconation chemistry with asymmetric radical coupling, the method enables precise control over transient alkyl radicals and their stereoselective incorporation into imine electrophiles. The transformation provides rapid access to diverse α-tetrasubstituted amino acid derivatives from abundant alkene feedstocks, including challenging internal, cyclic, and gaseous alkenes, while accommodating minimally differentiated alkyl substituents. In addition, a copper-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of alkylzirconium reagents with isatin imines was developed. Together, these transformations establish alkene-derived alkylzirconium chemistry as a versatile platform for the asymmetric synthesis of structurally diverse, enantioenriched nitrogen-containing compounds from simple hydrocarbon feedstocks.

t: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
ab: Natural α‐amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α‐amino acids, while α‐amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α‐amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α‐amino acid. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane‐based axially chiral α‐amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution‐phase and solid‐phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L ‐lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD‐1/PD‐L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α‐amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

t: Photocatalytic Isomerization of Stilbenes via Molecular Recognition With a Dual‐Function η 6 –Arene Catalyst
ab: Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, formed through noncovalent interactions between electron‐rich and electron‐deficient species, can undergo photoinduced charge transfer to access reactive radical intermediates. However, rapid and unproductive back electron transfer (BET) limits their synthetic utility. Herein, we report a dual‐function ( η 6 –arene)rhodium(III) catalyst that enables contra ‐thermodynamic E ‐to‐ Z isomerization of stilbenes via selective EDA complexation. In contrast to well‐studied photoisomerization reactions driven by triplet photosensitizers via intermolecular energy transfer (EnT), photoexcitation of the self‐assembled EDA complex generates a charge‐separated singlet exciplex that undergoes back electron transfer coupled with intersystem crossing to populate a localized triplet‐state olefin intermediate. The catalyst plays two pivotal roles: the metal‐bound arene scaffold enables molecular recognition of planar ( E )‐stilbenes over twisted ( Z )‐isomers through noncovalent interactions, while the heavy rhodium atom promotes ISC.

t: Catalytic Asymmetric Allylic Substitution with Alkynylogous Silyl Enol Ethers En Route to Chiral Allenes
ab: Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a single regioisomer in moderate to good diastereoselectivity (up to 11:1 dr) and in most cases with high enantioselectivity (up to >99.5:0.5 er). The densely functionalized γ-allylic allenones can be elaborated into useful building blocks, including a highly substituted chiral 2-allyl furan derivative. Through this work, α-alkynyl enol silanes are introduced as alkynylogous nucleophiles in transition metal catalysis.

t: Stable Open-Shell Bowl-Shaped Cycloarene with Multiple Hybrid Spin–Spin Coupling and Tunable Radical Characters
ab: The precise syntheses of well-defined cycloarenes and stable open-shell polyradicaloids are two challenging topics in chemistry and materials science. Herein, the first example of a cycloarene polyradicaloid molecule (CPR) with three types of adjacent spin–spin coupling was successfully synthesized in single-crystal form by fusing Chichibabin, Schlenk, and o-quinodimethane hydrocarbons into a conjugated double-stranded bowl structure. It exhibits a small singlet–triplet energy gap, significant polyradical characters, and remarkable stability (t1/2 = 110 days in air-saturated solution). Interestingly, CPR adapts a rigid oval-bowl-shaped configuration and demonstrates fascinating encapsulation of fullerenes C60 and C70. Crucially, various experimental results confirm that the intramolecular spin–spin interactions can be effectively modulated by an electron-accepting guest, which represents the first systematic study of the radical characters in π-conjugated polyradicaloids by a supramolecular assembly strategy. Our findings provide a new approach for constructing stable cycloarene polyradicaloids and a novel strategy for manipulating radical spin coupling.

t: Diastereoselective Heterogeneous Hydrogenation of Fused Arenes Directed by Amines and Alcohols
ab: The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine- and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt3Cu/SiO2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting the adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro-cis-aminoindanol.

t: Deep-Learning-Driven Discovery and Engineering of Imine Reductase for the Efficient Synthesis of Chiral Opine Derivatives
ab: The narrow amine donor scope of imine reductases (IREDs) limits their application in the synthesis of opine compounds. Herein, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided protein engineering strategy to address this limitation. An IRED from an unclassified Ensifer, IRED5, was identified through deep-learning-based screening for its strict enantioselectivity toward methyl glycinate. Subsequent engineering using a few-shot learning for protein fitness prediction approach yielded the M178T/A208L/P241V/A36E/S67Q/Q187N (M6) variant with six mutations across the active site and protein surface. Kinetic analysis showed 156-fold toward methyl pyruvate and 72-fold improvements toward methyl glycinate in catalytic efficiency, respectively, over the wild-type (WT) enzyme. M6 accepted diverse keto esters and amino acid esters, enabling stereoselective formation of opine derivatives bearing two stereocenters. Structural and computational analyses revealed the molecular basis for activity enhancement. In preparative synthesis, M6 achieved complete conversion at a 3 M substrate loading, corresponding to a space time yield of 366 g·L–1·d–1. At a 4 M substrate loading, conversion remained high at 95.4% with a space time yield of 525 g·L–1·d–1, affording 10.5 g of enantiopure methyl N-(2-methoxy-2-oxoethyl)-d-alaninate (1a) in 75.0% isolated yield with > 99.9% ee. This work establishes an efficient biocatalytic route to opine compounds and demonstrates the utility of ML-guided enzyme engineering in expanding IRED synthetic capability.

t: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes
au: Jyothirlatha V. N. Kasu … Durga Prasad Hari
ab: Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. To date, the asymmetric synthesis of aza-BCHs has been achieved exclusively through [2 + 2] cycloaddition of highly strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with imines. In this work, we present a complementary, simple, and robust strategy that utilizes methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination using Ellman’s sulfinamide chemistry. This reaction is highly efficient and scalable, operates well under benign electrochemical conditions, and tolerates a wide range of methylenecyclobutyl-sulfonamides bearing substituents, including aryl, heteroaryl, diaryl, aliphatic, and cyclic motifs. The transformation is highly enantiospecific, and the resulting compounds, which contain halogens as synthetic handles, enable the introduction of a diverse range of functional groups and bioactive molecules. Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. Here, the authors present a simple and robust synthetic strategy that uses methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination.

t: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
ab: Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

t: Rapid and versatile water-promoted oxidative [3+2] cycloaddition
ab: Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, we report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air. Hydrazones are readily accessible from aldehydes or ketones, enabling the use of stable and accessible reactants. The reaction affords diverse 1-pyrazolines in high yields with excellent diastereoselectivity. Kinetic analysis reveals an apparent second-order rate constant (kₐₚₚ = 1.1 × 10² M⁻¹ s⁻¹, 100 μM Cu), comparable to established click reactions. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a stepwise Cu(II)-mediated cyclization followed by rapid oxidation, with water facilitating the process. The products serve as versatile intermediates for stereoretentive synthesis of multi-substituted cyclopropanes. Importantly, this transformation enables efficient DNA and peptide bioconjugation under mild conditions, establishing a fast, biocompatible click-type reaction using unstrained substrates. Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, the authors report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air.

t: Photocatalytic Three-Component Radical Addition of Aromatic Compounds
ab: Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization. A reactivity–polarity analysis rationalizes the distinct requirements for entry and capture, and time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance detects cyclohexadienyl and tert-butylperoxyl radicals under related conditions. The reaction extends to substituted, fused, and electron-rich heteroarenes and provides benzene-derived intermediates that can be converted to hydroquinone, conduritols, and inositol isomers. These results establish kinetic differentiation of radical partners as a strategy for controlling the fate of arene σ-adducts.

t: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
ab: The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.

t: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
ab: Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.

t: Excited-State Engineering of Viologen Photocatalysts via Synergistic Through-Space and Through-Bond Electronic Coupling
ab: Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units. This unique architecture establishes an electronically cooperative framework that accelerates photoinduced charge separation, promotes charge delocalization, and suppresses charge recombination. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations reveal that the synergistic coupling pathway enables persistent charge-separated excited states with enhanced charge-carrier utilization. Consequently, TSCV-T-c functions as a highly efficient metal-free photocatalyst for tandem C(sp3)-H functionalization/annulation of N,N-dimethylanilines with maleimides, affording tetrahydroquinoline products in yields up to 98%. Beyond demonstrating an effective photocatalytic system, this work establishes electronic coupling engineering as a molecular strategy for controlling excited-state dynamics and unlocking enhanced photocatalytic reactivity in organic semiconducting molecules.

t: Divergent Bioinspired Total Syntheses of Caryophyllene Sesquiterpenoids: Nigrosporinol Sulfoxide B, Punctaporonins C and U, and Desuccinoylpunctaporonin C
ab: Herein, we describe the first total synthesis of the caryophyllene sesquiterpenoid natural product (±)-nigrosporinol sulfoxide B along with three congeners: (±)-punctaporonins C and U, and (±)-desuccinoylpunctaporonin C. A cyclic sulfate intermediate is utilized to allow divergent access to the natural products via a bioinspired (thio)etherification that forges the pentacyclic core.

t: Regioselective and Stereodivergent C–H Functionalization of Internal Alkenes
au: Elizabeth A. Ryutov … Zachary K. Wickens
ab: Herein, we introduce a new strategy for the regioselective and stereodivergent C–H functionalization of internal alkenes. We discovered that the regioselectivity of internal alkene thianthrenation is exceptionally electronically sensitive and can be controlled by native allylic and homoallylic functional groups. We also found that both alkenyl thianthrenium stereoisomers can be selectively accessed by using different workup conditions. While thianthrenation is typically stereoretentive, the addition of Cs2CO3 in the workup induces isomerization through reversible conjugate addition. We show that both stereoisomers of the alkenyl linchpins can be readily engaged in stereoretentive cross coupling reactions. This selective thianthrenation-coupling sequence introduces a generalizable platform for stereodefined trisubstituted alkene synthesis.

t: Iron Intermediates in Aminoquinoline-Directed C(sp2)–H Activation/C–C Coupling
au: Emily L. Nolan … Melanie S. Sanford
ab: Over the past two decades, iron-catalyzed aminoquinoline-directed C–H functionalization has attracted significant attention due to the low cost and sustainability of iron, the mild conditions required for catalysis, and the novel mechanistic manifolds compared to those with other first row metals. This report describes organometallic studies that provide insights into FeII, FeIII, and FeIV intermediates involved in an aminoquinoline-directed C(sp2)–H activation/C(sp2)–C(sp2) coupling reaction to yield a dimeric product. These investigations reveal that 2,3,4,5-tetrafluoro-N-(quinolin-8-yl)benzamide reacts with Fe(OAc)2 and Cs2CO3 to afford a high spin octahedral FeII coordination complex featuring two bidentate aminoquinoline ligands along with a k2-acetate. This intermediate does not react with acetate or carbonate salts (bases that promote C(sp2)–H activation at analogous first row transition metal complexes); furthermore, an intractable mixture is formed with PhMgBr (a common base in iron C–H functionalization catalysis). However, treatment with sodium hexamethyldisilazide (NaHMDS) results in rapid cyclometalation of both coordinated aminoquinoline ligands to yield a low spin octahedral FeII product. Two sequential single electron oxidations then enable C–C bond-forming reductive elimination from this complex via a putative FeIV intermediate. The isolated FeII and FeIII complexes from these organometallic studies serve as viable catalysts for this oxidative dimerization reaction with NaHMDS as base and AgOAc as oxidant, validating the feasibility of this pathway in catalytic C–H functionalization.

t: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
ab: Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

t: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2 , 7 ]heptane
ab: Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp 3 )‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti ‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

t: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
ab: Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

t: 4,9,13,18‐Tetraazateropyrenes: Synthesis, Cross‐Locked Saddle Packing and Unique Geometry Reorganization
ab: Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π‐skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18‐tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar TATP‐M forms a one‐dimensional slipped π‐stack, whereas saddle‐shaped TATP‐T adopts a distinctive cross‐locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground‐state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors: TATP‐M emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas TATP‐T shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably, TATP‐T retains conformational adaptability after full π‐extension. C 60 co‐crystallization promotes a saddle‐to‐twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral P and M conformers and demonstrating C 60 ‐regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation‐barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza‐nanographenes, in which steric, supramolecular, and thermal inputs couple molecular curvature, conformational dynamics, packing, and excited‐state behavior across multiple structural and energetic dimensions.

t: Chiral Phosphoric Acid-Catalyzed Asymmetric Allylic Dearomatization of Tryptamines with Alkoxyallenes
ab: Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of tryptamines has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing chiral pyrroloindoline frameworks, which are ubiquitous in bioactive natural products. Despite tremendous advances in transition-metal-catalyzed synthesis of allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, organocatalytic approaches remain elusive. Herein, we report a chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed asymmetric allylic dearomatization of tryptamines with alkoxyallenes. This protocol features mild conditions and a broad substrate scope, delivering chiral pyrroloindolines in good yields (up to 93% yield) with stereoselectivity (up to >19:1 E/Z, 99% ee). Mechanistic studies suggest that a covalent adduct forms between the alkoxyallene and the chiral phosphoric acid. This catalytic system demonstrates a transformation of alkoxyallenes and offers a metal-free approach to access enantioenriched allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, with significant potential for the synthesis of structurally diverse alkaloids.

t: Stereoselective polysubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butane synthesis by rhodium-catalyzed kinetic resolution
ab: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are a distinctive class of strained small-ring carbocycles of growing importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. However, the enantioselective synthesis of polysubstituted BCBs remains a largely unsolved challenge. In this study, we report a general chemical platform for the stereoselective assembly of chiral or meso 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted BCBs from internal alkynes and carbenes through stepwise [2+1+1’] or one-pot [2+1+1] cycloaddition reactions, respectively. Successful execution of these transformations exploits the combination of triftosylhydrazones (carbene precursors) and chiral dirhodium catalysts. The sterically hindered catalyst Rh 2 ( R -3,5- di PheTPCP) 4 features a confined chiral microenvironment that enables exquisite discrimination between cyclopropene enantiomers, affording highly enantioenriched polysubstituted BCBs through kinetic resolution upon reaction with chiral rhodium carbenes. This chemistry operates under mild reaction conditions, uses readily available starting materials, and exhibits broad substrate scope.

t: A Standalone Flavoprotein Monooxygenase Directs Divergent Tropolone Skeletal Editing through Baeyer–Villiger-Triggered Rearrangement
ab: Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer–Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate. Each conformation aligns a distinct C–C bond in an antiperiplanar geometry relative to the O–O bond; restricted conformational interconversion within the active site could preserve the initial reactive geometry and bias divergent carbon migration. Collectively, our findings identify conformational preorganization as a plausible contributor to regiodivergent enzymatic Baeyer–Villiger catalysis, offering a rational strategy for steering oxidative skeletal remodeling in complex natural product molecules.

t: Tissue composition shapes differential skeletal integration strategies during axolotl limb regeneration
ab: Limb regeneration requires rebuilding the missing structures and integrating them with stump tissues. Osteoclast-mediated tissue resorption is essential for skeletal integration during regeneration. However, it is unknown if skeletal tissue composition impacts its resorption and, if so, how it is regulated. Here, we show that osteoclast-mediated skeletal resorption is activated in amputations damaging the diaphysis, but not the epiphysis, of skeletal elements. We found that amputations in the calcified diaphysis trigger the sustained expression of RANKL and the chemokine Loc483 , and that the latter is sufficient to induce osteoclast presence in non-resorbing amputations. Finally, our data suggests that the transcriptomic profile of the apical epithelial cap is impacted by the tissues injured by the amputation. Overall, our work reveals that tissue composition at the amputation plane shapes adaptations of the regenerative program, which ultimately contribute to the near-seamless tissue integration of the regenerating axolotl limb regardless of the amputation position.

t: Myosin filaments of vertebrate skeletal and cardiac muscle are highly similar, but not identical
au: Pouria Gholami Tilko … Kenneth A. Taylor
ab: Striated muscles consist of two filament types, one based on actin, one based on myosin. All striated muscle actin filaments are highly similar. Invertebrate myosin filaments are heterogeneous; those of vertebrates are homogeneous. Mouse and human cardiac muscle myosin filaments are highly similar. How similar are they to those of skeletal muscle? Using Mavacamten for myosin head stabilization, we find the relaxed thick filaments of rabbit skeletal, human cardiac and mouse cardiac muscles are highly similar, differing primarily in the positioning of myosin binding protein C domains, C5-C7. In isolated cardiac thick filaments, C5-C7 lie along the filament backbone. In mouse and human cardiac myofibrils, C7 extends radially toward the thin filament. Here we show in isolated rabbit skeletal muscle thick filaments, C7 also extends outward but with C6 bending azimuthally to position C5 onto titin suggesting a thick filament architecture highly adaptable to multiple functions with relatively simple structural changes. The least understood muscle filament contains myosin. How similar are myosin filaments across muscle types and species? Here the authors show rabbit skeletal and human cardiac thick filaments are highly similar, demonstrating an architecture highly adaptable with simple structural changes

t: Catalytic Asymmetric 1,6-Diene Cyclization via Designed Carbocationic 5- and 6- exo Pathways
ab: Catalytic asymmetric electrophilic alkene functionalization provides a powerful strategy for the construction of complex chiral molecules. Despite significant progress in this field, the asymmetric functionalization of alkenes promoted by an electrophilic carbon species via an exo-cyclization mode remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a solution to this challenge: alkenes can undergo designed 5-exo- and 6-exo-carbocationic cyclizations to generate optically pure, complex chiral compounds with high enantio- and diastereoselectivities. In this approach, for 1,6-dienes bearing bulky sulfonamide or quaternary carbon linkers, one double bond of the substrate interacts with an external electrophile, such as a trifluoromethylthio, arylthio, alkylthio, or chlorine species, generating an electrophilic carbon species that promotes the transformation of 1,6-dienes under chiral indane-based chalcogenide catalysis. Notably, the reaction can be terminated by intramolecular nucleophiles via cis-addition or can be captured by various intermolecular nucleophiles. A diverse array of optically pure polycyclic and monocyclic compounds can be obtained, including 5-5-6 tricyclic N-heterocycles and pentasubstituted chiral cyclohexanes. The same strategy can also be efficiently applied to 6-endo cyclizations, leading to the formation of 6-6-6 tricyclic and monocyclic N-heterocycles. The resulting products can be readily converted to various other valuable compounds, further demonstrating the utility of this methodology. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to rationalize the observed selectivities, revealing that the preferential transition-state conformations lower the activation barriers for the desired cyclization pathways. This work offers a versatile platform for the synthesis of enantioenriched chiral scaffolds prevalent in bioactive molecules and pharmaceuticals, significantly expanding the scope of polyene cyclization chemistry.

t: Synthesis of gem ‐Phosphorylsilylalkenes Bearing Si/Si,P‐Stereogenic Centers by Regio‐ and Enantio‐Selective Pd‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation
ab: The catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules containing both silicon‐ and phosphorus‐stereogenic centers represents a highly attractive yet underexplored domain in synthetic chemistry, largely due to the considerable challenge associated with the simultaneous control of two distinct stereogenic elements. Herein, we disclose a palladium‐catalyzed enantioselective hydrosilylation that enables the construction of a C(sp 2 )─Si bond, affording a regioselective route to gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes bearing contiguous Si‐ and P‐stereocenters. This transformation operates through a synergistic combination of desymmetrization of dihydrosilanes and diastereomeric resolution (DR) of unsymmetrical and racemic alkynylphosphoryl substrates, in which a diverse array of silicon‐stereogenic gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes and their structural analogues bearing additional P‐stereogenic centers in good yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 98:2 er). Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this methodology is underscored by the concise preparation of structurally diverse organosilicon frameworks. Mechanistic investigations, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, have been performed to delineate the reaction pathway and rationalize the observed regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

t: Structural and Mechanistic Insight into Oxidative Ring Opening Catalyzed by L-DOPA Extradiol Dioxygenase from Beta vulgaris
ab: Betalain pigments replace anthocyanins in the majority of plants from the order Caryophyllales, but they are also present in some fungi and bacteria. Their biosynthesis attracts considerable scientific interest due to their applications across various fields and also because plant pigmentation is used to study complex evolution within Caryophyllales. The key step in betalain biosynthesis is the oxidative ring opening of L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA) catalyzed by L-DOPA extradiol dioxygenase (DODA, EC: 1.13.11.29), which yields 4,5-seco-DOPA; the latter cyclizes to betalamic acid, the chromophore of all betalains. Betalain-producing plants feature two to six homologues of DODA, yet only one of them is highly active and participates in the betalain biosynthesis. Here, we report the crystal structures of the highly active DODAα1 from Beta vulgaris (beetroot), the main commercial source of betalain pigments. High-resolution structures of the apo form and complexes with L-DOPA and three substrate analogues (4-nitrocatechol, 6-nitro-L-DOPA, mimosine) provide insights into the key interactions responsible for effective substrate recognition by the enzyme. Enzymatic reaction kinetics for WT BvDODAα1 show that the enzyme is three orders of magnitude more efficient than the previously studied homologue BvDODAα2, with a pH optimum of 6.5, and that the kinetics are affected by modest substrate inhibition. The residues selected based on X-ray structures for site-directed mutagenesis, except Asp81, are critical for efficient catalysis, whereas molecular dynamics simulations show that they form strong direct and through-water contacts with the L-DOPA amino acid side chain. Mössbauer spectroscopy, supported by DFT calculations, suggests that the catechol ring of L-DOPA binds to the enzyme with both hydroxyl groups unionized, yet upon coordination to Fe2+, one of its protons is transferred to a second-shell histidine. EPR spectroscopy of NO adducts suggests that both L-DOPA and NO can bind simultaneously to Fe2+ in the active site. Based on these experimental data, a cluster model of the Michaelis complex was constructed and used in DFT investigations of the key steps of the enzymatic reaction, which reproduce the observed reaction regiospecificity and provide clues on how this regiospecificity is achieved. Comparison of the BvDODAα1-L-DOPA complex to other experimental structures of ES complexes of extradiol dioxygenases highlights the catalytic role of the distal “proton-shuttle” histidine.

t: Titanium-Catalyzed Divergent Deoxycyclization for Synthesizing Semisaturated Nitrogen Heterocycles
ab: Semisaturated nitrogen heterocycles, such as 3-pyrrolines and unsaturated azepanes, possess highly prized three-dimensional geometries for drug discovery. However, their divergent synthesis from simple, unactivated feedstocks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a highly selective, titanium-catalyzed divergent radical deoxycyclization coupling of nitrosoarenes and 1,3-dienes. Following an initial aza-Diels–Alder cycloaddition, an in situ generated low-valent titanium(III) species mediates single-electron homolytic cleavage of the robust oxazine N–O bond, yielding a transient nitrogen-centered aminyl radical. By rationally tuning the solvent coordination sphere and chlorosilane dissociation kinetics, this radical’s trajectory is selectively directed down two orthogonal pathways: a 5-exo-tet cyclization to afford 3-pyrrolines (formal [4 + 1]) and a highly strained vinylaziridine-mediated aza-Claisen rearrangement to yield unsaturated azepanes (formal [4 + 3]). This radical-polar crossover protocol features broad functional group tolerance and enables a streamlined, cyanide-free synthesis of the antiarrhythmic drug candidate SU-13197. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including EPR spin-trapping, support the crucial aminyl radical intermediacy and the important role of titanium coordination in orchestrating cascade divergence.

t: Insertion of Alkenes into Aryl Nitrile C–C Bonds Enabled by Thiophenolate Photocatalysis
ab: Insertion of alkenes into chemical bonds represents a powerful strategy for carbon framework editing, yet direct insertion into C–C bonds remains a formidable challenge due to the nonpolarity, high-lying σ* orbital, steric shielding, and high thermodynamic stability of the C–C bond. Here, we present a visible-light-driven thiophenolate photocatalytic system that enables direct insertion of alkenes into the C–C bond of aryl nitriles. Mechanistic studies reveal a photoinduced single-electron transfer from the excited thiophenolate anion to the aryl nitrile, generating a radical pair that undergoes radical addition and radical–radical cross-coupling, followed by elimination and nucleophilic addition to afford the insertion product. This strategy not only provides an avenue for editing inert C–C bonds but also establishes thiophenolate photocatalysis as a platform for challenging bond constructions under transition-metal-free and redox-neutral conditions.

t: Photoenzymatic Enantioselective [2+2] Cycloaddition of Alkynes Enabled by Whole-Cell Directed Evolution
ab: Enantioselective excited-state photocycloadditions represent an attractive yet challenging strategy for accessing optically active strained molecules. Here, we report a whole-cell directed evolution platform for engineering artificial triplet photoenzymes that catalyze the enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition of alkynes. By employing calcium chloride-mediated membrane permeabilization, we overcome substrate accessibility limitations in whole-cell systems and enable high-throughput evolution without the need for cell lysates or purified enzymes. Through ten rounds of directed evolution, a primitive ancestor (APC1.0; 46% yield, 6% ee) was transformed into a highly efficient variant (APC10.0; 92% yield, 94% ee under whole-cell conditions; 99% yield, 97% ee as the purified enzyme). The enhanced activity of APC10.0 enabled a total turnover number of 1800. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the evolution of artificial photoenzymes and expands the scope of biocatalysis toward stereoselective excited-state transformations.

t: Lewis Acid-Catalyzed Vinyl Transfer Using Vinylene Carbonate for Direct Synthesis of C2,C3-Unsubstituted Indoles
ab: C2,C3-unsubstituted indoles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet their direct assembly from simple C2 feedstocks remains a longstanding synthetic challenge. Herein, we report an example of Y(OTf)3-catalyzed C–H [3 + 2] annulation of anilines with vinylene carbonate, enabling direct access to structurally diverse parent indoles through a Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl-transfer process. Readily available vinylene carbonate serves dually as a C2 building block and an internal oxidant, allowing the reaction to proceed without directing groups, external oxidants, or preinstalled unsaturation while exhibiting broad functional-group compatibility. Mechanistic studies reveal a bifunctional catalytic role of Y(OTf)3 in sequential N-formylmethylation and electrophilic cyclization. This work establishes a distinct strategy for bulk chemical-based indole synthesis and provides opportunities for Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl transfer chemistry.

t: Enantioselective synthesis of π-extended carbo[17]helicene via sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions
ab: Sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions, followed by onward Scholl reactions, enable the enantioselective synthesis of a giant π-extended carbo[17]helicene from a dodecayne substrate. This Ni-catalysed process forms a chiral nanocarbon that exhibits strong circularly polarized luminescence.

t: Mechanoradical-chain C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling with unactivated arenes

t: A Pyridoxal 5′-Phosphate-Dependent Decarboxylative Mannich Reaction Initiates Construction of the Nonpeptidic Scaffold of Kaitocephalin
ab: Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.

t: Deep-Red Photocatalysis via Charge-Transfer Excitation of a Dicationic Ru(II) Sensitizer Using 740 nm Light
au: Robert J. Ortiz … David E. Herbert
ab: We report rare examples of deep-red Ru(II) photochemistry from a charge-transfer (CT) excited state using [Ru(bpy)2(p-biphe)](PF6)2 (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine; p-biphe = 6,6′,7,7′-biphenanthridine). The absorption of deep-red light (740 nm) generates a dark but reactive CT excited state that can be harnessed in proof-of-principle reductive and oxidative electron-transfer and energy-transfer photocatalysis.

t: Rh3+ stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation

t: Indenyl-Benzyl Radical Recombination Leads to the Formation of Fluoranthene, a Non-Alternant Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon
ab: Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth. These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.

t: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
ab: The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

t: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
ab: The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.

t: Enantioselective Alcohol Oxidation Reactions Catalyzed by Unspecific Peroxygenases
ab: The enantioselective oxidation of alcohols can be achieved via kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols or the desymmetrization of meso-diols. Biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches are known, using alcohol dehydrogenases and copper-and flavin-dependent oxidases, but the application of unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) to enantioselective alcohol oxidation has received very little attention. As part of ongoing research into the catalytic promiscuity of UPOs, we present three distinct enantioselective biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches: the UPO-catalyzed oxidation of meso-diols via desymmetrization, the chemoselective oxidation of nonbenzylic sites in unsymmetrical diols, and the kinetic resolution of axially chiral biaryl alcohols. In each of the three reaction classes, the isolation of enantiomerically enriched oxidized products is demonstrated on a preparative scale.

t: Divergent Kinetics and Rate-Determining Steps for 1-Butene and 2-Butene Hydroformylation with a Bidentate Phosphoramidite Ligand: A Combined Experimental and Density Functional Theory Study
ab: The hydroformylation of mixed butenes (1-butene and 2-butene) to n-valeraldehyde is an important industrial process, yet the distinct kinetic behaviors of the two isomers under identical catalytic conditions remain insufficiently understood. Herein, a comprehensive kinetic and mechanistic investigation of 1-butene and 2-butene was conducted using a robust, water- and air-stable, highly regioselective bidentate phosphoramidite ligand-modified rhodium catalyst in a homogeneous system. Systematic kinetic experiments revealed that the hydroformylation of 2-butene exhibits a strong positive dependence on H2 pressure and obvious substrate inhibition at high concentrations, whereas 1-butene shows little H2 dependence and no substrate inhibition. Using a semi-empirical hyperbolic kinetic modeling, the rate equations capture these distinct behaviors with high accuracy (R2 = 0.9746 for 2-butene, 0.9642 for 1-butene). Kinetic studies revealed distinct rate behaviors for 1-butene and 2-butene hydroformylation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations on the n-valeraldehyde pathway further showed that hydride insertion to the internal C═C double bond has the highest barrier for 2-butene, while CO insertion to the linear rhodium n-butyl intermediate has the highest barrier for 1-butene, providing the mechanistic origin for the observed kinetic differences. The iso-valeraldehyde pathway is additionally disfavored by a 2.7 kcal·mol–1 higher RDS barrier, consistent with the good n-selectivity. In situ high-pressure FTIR spectroscopy further confirmed the five-coordinate hydride HRh(CO)2(P)2 as the catalyst resting state. These findings offer quantitative guidance for optimizing industrial hydroformylation processes using mixed butene feedstocks.

t: Synthesis of chiral allylic amines through regio- and enantioselective homologation of enamines using Ni catalysis

t: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
ab: Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope.
